notes: v289 (web-only, no native change) — FUEL-LIST-STALE (owner report Oct 30, 2026, 16:12 MDT: the Fuel Fill-ups list 'never up to date', newest entry 2026-10-22 though the truck fuelled Oct 24/26/29). ROOT CAUSE (proven, tools/fuel-list-stale-v289-test.js): pushOne's oversized guard (MAX_DOC_BYTES 900,000) ran BEFORE the v272 record-list read-merge-write and sealed the key clean while skipping the write. The fuel_fills value — the fill records with their receipt-photo data URLs inside — outgrew the cap on photos alone (~1.57 MB in the modeled 59-fill book), so from the day the book crossed the cap every push was skipped, the cloud copy froze at the last state that fit (Oct 22), and sync reported success. Fills kept saving locally; the Oct 30 install churn then restored the frozen cloud copy wholesale, erasing Oct 23-30 fills from phone and cloud alike — the same signature as FUEL-HISTORY-LOST-OCT20-22 and the Oct 26 recurrence (v241/v272 fixed the merge law, never the byte-cap ordering in front of it). FIX (cloudsync.js only): record-list keys no longer take the oversized skip; the record-list write carries a sync copy — for fuel_fills, when the book exceeds the cap, the same records without the photo field (facts complete; each fill's photo is also written to its own per-fill cloud doc by the Fuel save handler itself). Fuel identity (date/time/litres/cost/station/odo) never reads the photo, so merges, the shadow, the v188 Oct 15 duplicate rule and P&L are untouched; merge completeness (photo +3) means a pull can never strip a photo off the phone. A copy that still exceeds the cap fails honestly (key stays dirty, failure named) instead of sealing clean. The pull's union-vs-cloud comparison uses the sync copy, so a photo-bearing book seals for real after its push instead of re-pushing every cycle. HARNESS: tools/fuel-list-stale-v289-test.js 14/14 — RED on the v288 tree with his exact sequence (settled Oct-22 book over the cap -> saves Oct 24/26/29 -> zero cloud writes, false seal, fresh-boot restore lands on newest=2026-10-22), GREEN after.
